memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'This bread is to be set out before the LORD regularly, Sabbath after
Sabbath, on behalf of the Israelites, as a lasting covenant'"
- Lev 24:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Fresh bread every week. Not once a year at a great festival, but Sabbath
after Sabbath, in unbroken sequence. Somebody baked, somebody carried,
somebody arranged — every single week, for centuries.

That phrase "Sabbath after Sabbath" has a lovely ordinariness about it.
It is the sound of steady faithfulness. No drama, no announcement, just
the same good work done again.

Dear reader, our culture is fascinated by the extraordinary. We admire
the dramatic conversion, the powerful testimony, the church that grew
overnight. Scripture certainly records such things. But the tabernacle
was sustained by weekly repetition.

Your faithfulness may look very unremarkable to you. Family prayers
that get interrupted. The same offering given each month. Turning up to
the same small fellowship for years. Teaching the same children the same
truths.

Paul writes, let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper
time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up (Gal 6:9). He praised
the Thessalonians for their endurance inspired by hope (1 Thess 1:3).

Note also that God called this a lasting covenant. He binds Himself to
faithfulness first. Our steady obedience is only a small echo of His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has my faithfulness felt too ordinary to matter?
2. What good habit am I tempted to abandon because it feels repetitive?
3. How does God's own faithfulness encourage mine?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You are faithful Sabbath after Sabbath, year after year. Give me
endurance in the ordinary and keep me from growing weary in doing good.
Amen.
